_doc: Batch m02 (medium, opus themed pass): termite-column, leafcutter-column, army-ant-column, paper-wasp, hornet-sentry, mud-dauber, carpenter-bee, lantern-glowworm-queen, earwig-matron, luna-moth. Every piece has a hand note and an explicit motif. New motifs (19, all 10 signatures unique) are drawn by claude/pf-anim/motifs/medium_m02.js; reused catalogue motifs: pincer-snap (earwig-matron, sibling of earwig), mud-flop (mud-dauber b2).

termite-column.notes: Termite column: pale soft workers and big brown-headed soldiers that drum their heads, building clay mound spires; they travel in tunnels.

b0.n: Soldier Head Pinch: brown soldier heads push out into a jaw fence and pinch, click marks

b1.n: Column Jaw Surge: a file of soldiers surges along the edge, heads drumming

b2.n: Mud-Tube Shell: clay spires wall the edge while workers plaster, soil clods tossed up

b3.n: Tunnel Crawl Slip: workers vanish and pop up at new spots; the chain tunnels under the felt

u0.n: Mound Wall: clay spires rise one by one into a mound wall along the edge

u1.n: Soldier Bite: big-headed soldiers lunge off the edge, jaws snapping, dust kicked up

u2.n: Clay Armour: baked clay spires bristle out like a hard crust, dust blowing

u3.n: Tunnel Crowd: a crowd of soldiers bursts out of the ground and slams back, clods flying

leafcutter-column.notes: Leafcutter column: rust ants marching under raised green leaf pieces; scissor jaws cut crescents (they chirp as they cut).

b0.n: Leaf-Bearer Nip: bearers dip out from under their leaves and nip

b1.n: Opinionated Sting: snipping jaws lunge out, little anger marks above them

b2.n: Leaf Parade Shield: raised leaf pieces line the edge like a row of parasols

b3.n: Column Scatter: the column breaks up, bearers vanish in dust puffs and reappear

u0.n: Leaf Shears: scissor jaws cut along the edge in one line, leaf crescents flutter down

u1.n: March On: the leaf column marches on along the edge in one unbroken file

u2.n: Leaf Roof: cut leaf crescents overlap along the edge like roof tiles

u3.n: Green Parade: the parade swings out round the edge and back, leaves bobbing

army-ant-column.notes: Army ants: dark-red ants with huge pale sickle jaws in an endless flooding file; at rest they hook together into a living wall.

b0.n: Column Mandible Rush: sickle-jawed ants rush off the edge in waves

b1.n: Flood Ant Stab: the flood surges the length of the edge, jaws first

b2.n: Nest-Less Plating: ant bodies hook into a living plate along the edge

b3.n: Obstacle-Skirt Flow: the swarm skips spot to spot, flowing round whatever is in the way

u0.n: Column Wall: the bivouac wall bristles out, a fence of hooked jaws

u1.n: Flank Slip: the column splits round both flanks and closes up again

u2.n: Mandible Wave: a wave of huge jaws slams out and drops back, dust thrown up

u3.n: Endless File: the file never stops pouring along the edge, prey crumbs left behind

paper-wasp.notes: Paper wasps: slim amber wasps that fly with long legs dangling, guarding an open grey paper comb.

b0.n: Short Fuse Jab: a wasp jabs out legs-first and is back in a blink, sting lines

b1.n: Striped Lunge: one striped wasp lunges the length of the edge, legs trailing

b2.n: Papery Nest Guard: grey paper cells build up along the edge, an egg in each

b3.n: Sudden Flare Dart: wasps flare up at new spots and zigzag between them

u0.n: Wasp Sting: wasps drop sting-first off the edge, sting lines flashing

u1.n: Paper Nest: the open comb bristles out cell by cell, a shield of paper

u2.n: Buzz Dive: wasps dive off the edge with legs swinging

u3.n: Nest Hum: wasps fan out from the comb, hover humming and settle back

hornet-sentry.notes: Hornet sentry: big orange-brown hornets with dark eyes pacing at the round door of a scalloped paper nest.

b0.n: Doorway Dive: hornets launch out of the nest door one after another

b1.n: Night-Watch Strike: a sentry sweeps the edge under a moon glint

b2.n: Nest Door Bulwark: scalloped envelope bands line the edge round a dark door

b3.n: Blossom Snub: hornets blink from spot to spot shaking off pollen

u0.n: Nest Tending: fresh paper bands rise as the nest is patched, wood fibre falling

u1.n: Sentry Sting: the sentry runs the edge sting-first, sting lines flashing

u2.n: Paper Wall: the envelope's scalloped layers hold the edge, chewed wood fibre drifting

u3.n: Door Bar: sentries stand shoulder to shoulder across the door, pacing and turning

mud-dauber.notes: Mud dauber: slim black thread-waisted wasps hauling mud balls and building organ-pipe mud tubes.

b0.n: Mud Pipe Nip: black wasps dart out from their pipes and nip

b1.n: Wasp Needle Stab: a thread-waisted wasp needles along the edge, sting lines

b2.n: Mud Plaster Coat: mud splats slap onto the edge and flatten

b3.n: Rain-Dodge Hover: wasps blink between dry spots, raindrops flung off

u0.n: Mud Plaster: organ-pipe tubes grow ring by ring along the edge, wet mud sliding

u1.n: Pipe Jab: mud pipes jab out and drop back, wet beads flicking

u2.n: Nest Sealing: wasps press mud balls into the edge like spikes, clods flicked off

u3.n: Pipe Stack: a row of pipes stacks up along the edge in one line

carpenter-bee.notes: Carpenter bee: round glossy blue-black bee that hovers then darts, drilling perfectly round holes in wood.

b0.n: Carpenter Mandible Snip: glossy bees dart out and snip, sawdust spraying

b1.n: Needle Stinger: one glossy bee runs the edge stinger first

b2.n: Glossy Carapace: round blue-black bees hold the edge, a gloss streak running over them

b3.n: Hover Dart: a bee hangs in the air, then darts to the next spot

u0.n: Wood Drill: round bore holes drill along the edge in one line, sawdust spinning out

u1.n: Nectar Sip: bees rise from the edge dusted with yellow pollen

u2.n: Sawdust Cover: bees scatter into a cloud of falling sawdust and come back

u3.n: Hollow Tap: the bee knocks at its holes, they jump out and back with tap marks

lantern-glowworm-queen.notes: Glowworm queen: big glowing lamps swinging on long threads over a curtain of beaded silk in a mountain cave.

b0.n: Ceiling Lamp Bite: lamps swing out on their threads and snap at the edge

b1.n: Queen's Thread Lash: long glowing threads lash off the edge

b2.n: Silk Lamp Cocoon: a curtain of beaded threads hangs along the edge

b3.n: Bait Dangle Drop: a lamp bait blinks from thread to thread

u0.n: Lantern Lure: lamps lower on their threads and drip sticky glowing beads

u1.n: Queen Strike: the queen's big lamp runs the edge on its thread

u2.n: Thread Curtain: the curtain threads bristle out, beads sliding to the tips

u3.n: Ceiling Drop: the biggest lamp drops on its thread, slams and springs back

earwig-matron.notes: Earwig matron: a big chestnut earwig mother guarding and licking a clutch of pale eggs; shares the earwig forceps (pincer-snap) in her palette.

b0.n: Matron Pincer Clamp: big chestnut forceps lunge out and clamp

b1.n: Brood Guard Lunge: her forceps sweep the edge in front of the brood

b2.n: Egg Cradle Shield: pale egg clutches line the edge, jostled as she shields them

b3.n: Clutch Decoy: egg clutches blink at decoy spots

u0.n: Brood Tend: eggs rise licked clean, little shines blinking on them

u1.n: Egg Shell Ward: forceps bristle out over the clutch like a ring of spikes

u2.n: Matron Pincer: forceps clamp at spots, tied together in a snare line

u3.n: Egg Cushion: soft eggs settle along the edge in a cushion, soft puffs

luna-moth.notes: Luna moth: huge pale green wings with purple leading edges and eyespots, long trailing tails, flying by moonlight.

b0.n: Lantern Ribbon Sweep: moths sweep off the edge trailing their long tail ribbons

b1.n: Milk-Pale Gust: a wingbeat gust blows pale crescents and scale powder off

b2.n: Table-Mat Wing Shield: wings spread flat along the edge like table mats

b3.n: Lantern Glow Decoy: eyespot moths flash at decoy spots

u0.n: Moon Veil: pale crescents drift out in a haze and draw back

u1.n: Trailing Tails: moths swirl out and back, tails streaming

u2.n: Wing Buffet: huge pale wings slam out, scale powder bursting

u3.n: Lunar Hush: moon crescents hang still along the edge in a quiet haze
